Subject: Discovery recap & eval kickoff: Redwood trial plan

Hi Olivia / Samir —

Great to meet this morning — thanks for the walkthrough of Acme's recommendation pipeline and the latency/cost pain points you shared. Quick recap from our side and a proposed next step: an evaluation kickoff where we define the trial plan, success criteria, and the prompt/eval set we'll use to validate quality.

Discovery highlights:
- Primary workload: user-facing recommendations (re-rank + contextualization) with 2k median tokens per session.
- SLOs: 95th pct latency < 350ms, cost target ~40% lower than current infra.
- Data: small anonymized sample will be sufficient for prompt-level evals; engineering will need to validate access method (S3 vs secure upload).

Proposed evaluation kickoff goals:
1) Align on evaluation objectives & success metrics
2) Lock down prompt set and sample dataset to run gatekeeper evals
3) Confirm technical access (network, schema, sample artifacts) and personnel for the trial
4) Schedule demo/technical deep-dive and set timeline (2-4 week trial typical)

Availability for a 60–90 minute kickoff next week (PST):
- Tue 24 Feb: 10:00–11:30 or 14:00–15:30
- Wed 25 Feb: 09:00–11:00
- Thu 26 Feb: 13:00–15:00

I've attached a one-page eval plan and a draft SOW to give structure to the kickoff (redwood-eval-plan.pdf, SOW-draft-v1.pdf).

If those slots don't work, tell me a couple options and we'll align. Dev (cc'd) will run the technical portion; Ben (cc'd) will handle commercial/contract questions.

Thanks — look forward to getting this scheduled.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

Attachments: redwood-eval-plan.pdf, SOW-draft-v1.pdf

Hi all — quick note from the engineering side on agenda and prep items for the 90-minute kickoff:

- Architecture overview: endpoints, model variant recommendations, quantization/throughput tradeoffs
